threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground' when you're hopping from Dalston Junction to Hackney Central. It’s a tell.
Heard a bloke on the 37 bragging about his collection of 'rare' train tickets. Only in Brixton at 2 AM, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the old guy with a parrot on his shoulder arguing with a street musician about who plays better tunes on Hermannplatz.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Ever noticed how the kebab shops here stay open til dawn? It's like the unofficial after-party scene, with everyone sharing a late-night döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals can tell you which taco truck is worth the wait and which is just Instagram bait. The scent of al pastor is the ultimate test.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 bus today, and a musician was belting out 'California Dreamin''—totally drowned out the engine noises. Classic San Francisco vibe on a dreary day.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the side streets with old workshops that tell the real story of this neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look for a parking spot when they see a bike lane—like it's an unfamiliar landscape.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver doesn't say 'please' or 'thank you' after you've boarded. Locals just nod and find a seat.
Caught a glimpse of a fox rummaging through someone's takeaway bag on the 333. Only in Brixton do the late-night snacks attract wildlife.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found out my favorite Kebab shop also sells homemade baklava. It's like the hidden gems here just keep on coming.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find spontaneous parties in the park, where a DJ sets up in the middle of the afternoon with a crowd of dancing neighbors.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they navigate BART delays like they're dodging pigeons—no panic, just a resigned laugh and a quick pivot to tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that rolled up to a crowd of folks, but the driver just nodded and sped off—classic Tenderloin. Some didn't even flinch.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks and bars, but it’s the small, old shops and their owners that keep the real charm alive.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overly enthusiastic attempts to order 'café con leche' without a hint of an accent—it’s charming but cringy.
